source.title: AI Engram: In Search of Memory Traces in Artificial Intelligence
source.authors: Jea Kwon; Dong-Kyum Kim; Jiwon Kim; Yonghyun Kim; W. Kook; Meeyoung Cha

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates its own engram-based unlearning and discusses latent representations, but does not test whether the recovery attacks in the claim restore knowledge after unlearning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no recovery test using fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt changes. It does report representation-level DA and NMI results for its own method on image-class unlearning; these concern residual latent information but do not measure recovery or whether an attack succeeds.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a closed-form unlearning method (Engram) and reports forget/retain accuracy, TOFU metrics, membership-inference privacy scores and representation metrics (DA, NMI, CKA). It runs no recovery attack: no relearning fine-tuning, no direction ablation, no quantization, and no rephrasing or jailbreak prompts. Its claim that DA/NMI show traces are dissolved rather than masked concerns its own method's representations and is not a recovery test. So it does not test any version. It also does not claim robustness to the listed attacks, so F is not tested either.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add that representation metrics (DA, NMI) confirm Engram dissolves forget-set traces rather than masking outputs. They also say Engram trails iterative LLM methods (NPO, SimNPO, AltPO) on Overall and Privacy, and they position it as a complementary closed-form regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a retrospective, covariance-based weight edit; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks or unlearning recipes named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different results for α = 1 and αBEST in its CIFAR comparisons and uses an adaptive W-Norm scaling variant in its LLM experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Representation-level DA, NMI and CKA for Engram class-wise unlearning on CIFAR-10/100 are compared with retrained models. The authors read these as showing structural traces dissolved, not merely masked.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Closed-form covariance-projection unlearning yields forget-set representations close to a retrained model's.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper does not test any of the specified recovery attacks. Its representation-level evidence is from image-class unlearning and does not establish whether forgotten knowledge can be recovered.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant attack results were reported. Other unlearning performance metrics do not test the specified recovery behaviors.

untested.parts: Near-chance forget accuracy with preserved utility is shown for Engram on CIFAR/ImageNet/TOFU. No simple attack is tried to check whether the knowledge is recovered.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery test.
No activation-direction ablation. The DA/NMI/CKA analysis concerns Engram's own residual representation and does not show blocking versus deletion for any method.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery test.
Engram is not evaluated against any recovery attack, and the paper makes no robustness claim.

record.verdict_notes: TOFU results (Tables 3, 4, 6, 8, 9) and the MIA privacy scores are unlearning-efficacy measures, not recovery attacks, so leaving them out of the rows is appropriate. This is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after targeted accuracy is reduced.
No small-set or other post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery test.
No activation-direction ablation recovery test, nor an analysis showing that an existing unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
No test of a method’s resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: The paper interprets DA as alignment of forget-set features with the retain-set principal subspace. This is a representation-level result, not a test of recovery.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: The paper describes NMI as clustering separability between forget and retain features. It does not measure whether a recovery attack can retrieve forgotten knowledge.
rows.check: NMI is lower-is-better. Engram αBEST (0.611) is further from retrain (0.410) than Engram α=1 (0.379). That undercuts the paper's reading that traces are dissolved, but the row still does not bear on any version.
